messages:
anna: FYI ran into an auth precedence bug in the Python SDK on Windows when multiple Client instances are created with explicit api_key values. Thought it was rotation at first but repro is simpler.

anna: Minimal repro I used:
```python
from redwood import Client
c1 = Client(api_key="key-A")
c2 = Client(api_key="key-B")
print(c1._api_key, c2._api_key)  # expected key-A key-B but both show env value
```

anna: With REDWOOD_API_KEY set in the environment both clients pick it instead of the explicit param. Observed on native Windows and also on WSL.

mike: ugh. can you paste exact env + stdout? i'll try on mac/linux.

anna: steps:
1) set REDWOOD_API_KEY=env-KEY
2) run snippet above
3) stdout: env-KEY env-KEY

anna: also captured a network trace: Authorization header for both requests is `Bearer env-KEY` even after creating c1 with key-A.

jess: our docs state precedence is: explicit param > env var > config file. If code behaves differently it's a doc or code bug. thanks for reporting.

kevin: likely culprit: our AuthProvider reads env at module import into a module-level singleton. Client.__init__ currently defers to that singleton if present. On Windows the import timing/loader makes the singleton sticky and wins over init args.

kevin: quick workaround: explicitly set the transport header after creating the client:
```python
c = Client()
c._transport.default_headers.update({"Authorization": f"Bearer {your_key}"})
```
Not ideal but works until we ship a fix.

sam: this also happens in async flows. I hit a race where multiple async tasks create clients with different keys concurrently; because provider state is module-level and we mix contextvars, clients get the same key.

mike: can you drop a failing test or gist? i'll open an issue and assign to eng/clients.

anna: uploaded tiny repro gist: https://gist.github.com/anon/ef12ab34 (includes sync + asyncio cases).

mike: created issue #4916 assigned to @kevin and labeled python-sdk, auth, priority-high. please add PR when ready.

kevin: plan: change AuthProvider so Client.__init__ first checks explicit api_key arg and sets instance-level key before consulting any global provider. remove module-import-time env capture. add unit tests for precedence and an async concurrency test that spawns N tasks each creating Client(api_key=...) and asserting distinct keys.

jess: i'll also make a small docs patch clarifying precedence and include the Windows caveat.

deploy-bot: CI for #4916 triggered  build queued (linux, macos, windows).

sam: after the fix can we add an integration test that sets REDWOOD_API_KEY and creates two clients in parallel? that would have caught this earlier.

kevin: adding both unit + integration tests. Also adding a small stress test that repeatedly constructs/destroys clients under a mocked env to catch regressions.

anna: thanks everyone. temp mitigation: unset REDWOOD_API_KEY in your shell when running multi-client tests or use the header override. :thumbsup:
